sections.title: 2. Build Heap ( From an Existing Array )

blocks.text: In the last chapter, we learned what a heap is and its basic properties. Now let’s move on to the core operations that we perform on a heap.
1.1 Insert (Add a New Element)
New element always goes to the end of the array first. Then it bubbles up until the heap property is restored.
This bubbling up is called sift up or heapify up.
Step 1: Add at the end
Insert 0 at the end of the array → [1, 3, 2, 8, 5, 0]
/engineering/dsa-media/1785406367110-410164560.png
Step 2 Compare with parent
Check parent of0(which is2)
Since0 < 2, swap them →[1, 3, 0, 8, 5, 2]
/engineering/dsa-media/1785406367110-787739791.png
Step 3: Move up again
Now compare0with its new parent (1)
Since0 < 1, swap again →[0, 3, 1, 8, 5, 2]
/engineering/dsa-media/1785406367788-536647816.png
Simple:
Insert the new element at the end of the array, then compare it with its parent and swap if it is smaller.
Repeat this process (heapify up) until the heap property is satisfied or it becomes the root.
Time: O(log n):  tree height is log n, sift up traverses at most that many levels.
1.2 Extract Min ( Remove the Root )
The minimum is always at the root. But you can't just delete the root the tree would break into two.
The trick:

items: Step 1: Swap the root with the last element
Step 2: Remove the last element (old root)
Step 3: Sift the new root downward until the heap property is restored

blocks.text: This downward movement is called sift down or heapify down.
Step 1: Swap root with last element
Current heap array:[1, 3, 2, 8, 5, 4]
We always remove the root (minimum), but before removing it, we swap it with the last element.

Swap 1 (root) with 4 (last element):
→ [4, 3, 2, 8, 5, 1]
Step 2: Remove last element (old root)

Now remove the last element (which was the original root 1):
→ [4, 3, 2, 8, 5]
Extracted value = 1
Step 3: Sift down (heapify down)
Now 4 is at the root, but it may violate the min heap property.
Compare 4 with its children:
Choose the smaller child → 2

Since 4 > 2, swap them:
→ [2, 3, 4, 8, 5]
Now 4 is at index 2.
Check its children:
No children exist → it's a leaf node, So we stop here.
Explain:
We started with a min heap where the smallest element (1) is at the root. To delete it, we first swapped it with the last element (4) so that removal becomes easy.
Then we removed the last element, which was the original root (1), so 1 is now extracted and the heap size is reduced.
After removal, 4 came to the root, which may break the min heap property.

So we performed heapify down: we compared 4 with its children (3 and 2), picked the smaller child (2), and since 4 was larger, we swapped them. Now 4 moved down and became a leaf node, so no further action was needed.
The heap property is restored, and we successfully removed the minimum element.
Time: O(log n) sift down traverses at most log n levels.

Peek: Get Minimum Without Removing

In a min heap, the smallest element is always at the root, so we don’t need to do any changes or operations. 

We simply return the first element of the array, i.e., arr[0], and the heap remains unchanged.

content.title: 2. Build Heap ( From an Existing Array )

blocks.text: You have an unsorted array and want to turn it into a heap.

items: Naive approach: insert elements one by one → O(n log n).
Better approach: heapify in place from the bottom up.

blocks.text: We are trying to build a min heap from the array [8, 3, 5, 1, 7, 2]. Instead of starting from the root, we start from the last non-leaf node, because leaf nodes are already valid heaps.
The last non-leaf index is n/2 - 1 = 2. At index 2, value is 5. It has one child 2 (index 5). Since 5 > 2, we swap them → [8, 3, 2, 1, 7, 5].
Now move to index 1 (value 3). Its children are 1 and 7. Smallest child is 1, and since 3 > 1, swap → [8, 1, 2, 3, 7, 5].

Finally at index 0 (value 8). Its children are 1 and 2. Smallest is 1, so swap → [1, 8, 2, 3, 7, 5]. Now 8 is at index 1, compare with its children (3, 7), smallest is 3, so swap → [1, 3, 2, 8, 7, 5].
Now the array satisfies the min heap property.
/engineering/dsa-media/1785406367791-498306866.png
blocks.alt: Build Heap From an Existing Array

blocks.text: Time: O(n) surprisingly, building from scratch is linear.
In interviews you almost never build a heap from scratch. Use the built-in:

codes.python:
import heapq

min_heap = []

heapq.heappush(min_heap, 8)     # insert
heapq.heappush(min_heap, 3)
heapq.heappush(min_heap, 5)

print(min_heap[0])              # get min -> 3  (no removal)
print(heapq.heappop(min_heap))  # extract min -> 3
print(len(min_heap))            # 2
